problem:
A company produces two types of products, type A and type B. The revenue function of the company, in thousands of dollars, is given by $f:{R}^{2}\to R,$ defined as

$$
f(x)=-{y}^{4}-5{x}^{2}{y}^{2}+10{y}^{2}-2{x}^{2}+2,
$$

where $x={[\begin{aligned}\,x & y\,\end{aligned}]}^{T},$ $x$ is the price (in thousands of dollars) per unit of product A, and $y$ is the price (in thousands of dollars) per unit of product B. The company can adjust the prices per unit for both types of products by adding or removing certain features.

feedback.worked_solution:
For our scalar function, we have that

$$
{f}^{′}(x)={(∇f)}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}].
$$

Earlier, we found that 

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂y}=-4{y}^{3}-10{x}^{2}y+20y.
$$

The partial derivative of $f$ with respect to $x$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-{y}^{4}-5{x}^{2}{y}^{2}+10{y}^{2}-2{x}^{2}+2)=-10x{y}^{2}-4x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\,-10x{y}^{2}-4x\, & \,-4{y}^{3}-10{x}^{2}y+20y\end{aligned}].
$$
